━━ STEP 2 — INDIA-CALIBRATED SCORE (build from 0; apply mandatory deductions last) ━━

【A】 PROFITABILITY /20 — benchmarked vs Nifty 50 averages
ROE sub-score /7:
  +7 ROE ≥ 20% (top-quartile Indian company, well above Nifty avg 14-16%)
  +5 ROE 15-19% (at or above Nifty average — solid)
  +3 ROE 10-14% (below Nifty avg; acceptable for capital-intensive sectors)
  +1 ROE 5-9% (weak for a listed company)
   0 ROE < 5%, negative, or PAT loss
ROCE sub-score /7 (compare vs WACC hurdle of 12-14%):
  +7 ROCE ≥ 20% (generating real returns well above cost of capital)
  +5 ROCE 15-19%
  +3 ROCE 12-14% (just covering WACC — neutral)
  +1 ROCE 8-11% (destroying marginal value)
   0 ROCE < 8%
Net Margin sub-score /6 (Nifty 50 aggregate net margin ~12-14%):
  +6 Net Margin > 18% (exceptional — IT/FMCG quality)
  +4 Net Margin 10-18% (in line with Nifty 50 aggregate)
  +2 Net Margin 4-9% (thin; typical for trading, distribution, commodity)
   0 Net Margin < 4%
  DEDUCT -2 if OPM contracted > 150 bps YoY (margin erosion signal)

【B】 VALUATION /20 — compare ONLY vs relevant NSE sector median P/E above
P/E vs sector median /8:
  +8 P/E > 25% below sector median (materially cheap for the sector)
  +5 P/E within ±15% of sector median (fairly valued)
   0 P/E 15-35% above sector median (premium; needs growth justification)
  -4 P/E 35-60% above sector median with EPS growth < 20% (unjustified premium)
  -6 P/E > 2× sector median (speculative valuation; not grounded in earnings)
  NOTE: For banks/NBFCs use P/B vs sector median instead of P/E.
P/B vs ROE quality /6:
  +6 P/B ≤ 2× with ROE ≥ 18% (undervalued quality — rare in Indian market)
  +4 P/B 2-4× with ROE ≥ 15% (reasonable; in line with quality Indian franchises)
  +1 P/B 2-4× with ROE 10-14% (average; modest quality at fair price)
   0 P/B > 4× with ROE < 15% (value-trap risk)
  -3 P/B > 6× with ROE < 12% (pure speculative premium)
EV/EBITDA /6 (Indian quality names typically trade 15-30×):
  +6 EV/EBITDA < 10× (cheap even by Indian standards)
  +3 EV/EBITDA 10-18× (fair for Indian market)
   0 EV/EBITDA 18-28× (stretched; only justified for >20% growth compounders)
  -4 EV/EBITDA > 28× (expensive even vs Indian growth stocks)

【C】 FINANCIAL HEALTH /20 — calibrated for Indian corporate debt norms
Debt/Equity /8 (Indian cos historically carry more leverage than Western peers):
  +8 D/E < 0.25 (conservatively financed; strong signal in capex-heavy India)
  +5 D/E 0.25-0.75 (healthy across most Indian sectors)
  +2 D/E 0.75-1.5 (moderate; stress-test with interest coverage)
  -4 D/E 1.5-3.0 (high; flag in any non-infra, non-NBFC context)
  -8 D/E > 3.0 (distressed territory; common pre-cursor to defaults)
  EXCEPTION: Banks/NBFCs skip D/E — use Tier-1 CAR: ≥15% = +8, 12-15% = +4, <12% = -4.
Interest Coverage /7 (anchor: India 10-yr G-Sec ~7%; safe floor is 4× not 8×):
  +7 Coverage > 8× (very comfortable; can absorb rate hikes)
  +5 Coverage 4-8× (safe by Indian standards; most Nifty companies here)
  +2 Coverage 2-4× (marginal; watch for any debt rollover risk)
  -5 Coverage 1-2× (debt service stress; one bad quarter is dangerous)
  -8 Coverage < 1× (technical default risk; likely to dilute equity)
Current Ratio /5 (Indian working capital norms; manufacturing typically 1.2-1.8×):
  +5 Current Ratio > 2.0× (comfortable liquidity buffer)
  +3 Current Ratio 1.5-2.0×
  +1 Current Ratio 1.0-1.5× (tight but manageable)
  -4 Current Ratio < 1.0× (liquidity crunch)

【D】 GROWTH QUALITY /20 — benchmarked vs India nominal GDP 10-12%
Revenue Growth /8 (use 3-yr CAGR if available; else TTM YoY):
  +8 Revenue growth > 20% (compounding well above economy — strong)
  +5 Revenue growth 12-20% (ahead of or at India nominal GDP — decent)
  +2 Revenue growth 8-11% (pacing the economy — uninspiring)
   0 Revenue growth 4-7% (lagging the economy — structural concern)
  -3 Revenue declining (severe red flag in a 10-12% nominal growth economy)
EPS Growth /7:
  +7 EPS growth > 20% consistently (operating leverage + volume growth)
  +5 EPS growth 12-20%
  +2 EPS growth 8-11%
   0 EPS growth < 8% or flat
  -4 EPS declining despite revenue growth (margin compression, dilution, or tax anomaly)
Free Cash Flow /5:
  +5 FCF positive and growing YoY (high-quality earnings; not just accounting profit)
  +2 FCF positive but flat or lumpy (capex cycle)
  -3 FCF negative for 2+ consecutive years (cash-burning; question the business model)

【E】 TECHNICAL + GOVERNANCE /20 — NSE/BSE context
Price vs moving averages /8:
  +5 Price > 200DMA (institutional uptrend confirmed on NSE)
  -5 Price < 200DMA (institutional distribution; avoid catching falling knife)
  +3 50DMA > 200DMA (golden cross: momentum confirmed)
  -3 50DMA < 200DMA (death cross: momentum broken)
RSI-14 /3:
  +3 RSI 40-65 (healthy momentum; not extended)
  -3 RSI > 75 (overbought; high NSE circuit-filter risk on correction)
  -2 RSI < 30 (distressed selling; only positive if fundamentals clearly support)
Price vs 52W range /3:
  +3 Within 8% of 52W high with above-average volume (institutional accumulation)
  -2 Within 8% of 52W low on above-average volume (distribution)
Promoter pledging /4 (SEBI's most-watched governance metric for Indian investors):
  +4 Pledge = 0% with promoter holding ≥ 40% (fully aligned, no collateral pressure)
  +2 Pledge < 5%
  -3 Pledge 10-25% (moderate forced-sale risk; monitor quarterly)
  -6 Pledge 25-50% (high risk; historically source of price crashes — DHFL, Zee, ADAG)
  -8 Pledge > 50% (extreme distress; forced selling likely)
SEBI & ESG governance /2:
  +2 BRSR filed + credible ESG disclosures + no SEBI adverse action
  -3 Any pending SEBI show-cause notice or enforcement action

MANDATORY DEDUCTIONS (apply to sum after all category scores; these override positives):
  -12 Active SEBI enforcement, NCLT insolvency, or ED/CBI investigation
  -10 Auditor resignation, forensic audit flag, or qualified audit opinion in last 24 months
  -8 Receivables growing > 2× faster than revenue for 3+ quarters (revenue quality red flag)
  -7 Three consecutive quarters of simultaneous revenue AND margin decline
  -6 Promoter pledge > 35% of their total holding
  -5 Interest coverage < 1.5× (imminent debt stress given Indian credit market rates)
  -4 Promoter salary or related-party payments > 15% of net profit (wealth extraction)
